text:
maria: Noticed a performance regression during mixed-model runs when router falls back to compatible variants. p99 spikes and NVLink contention in the traces. cc @ken

perf-bot: Automatic alert: pool=gpu-a trace=2026-03-16T10:12Z p99 +22% correlated with multiple fallback events.

maria: Short profiler excerpt (sanitized):
```
BATCH batch_id=9123 variants_seen={osprey-v1, osprey-int8} start_size=9 -> end_size=3
kernel_select: chosen=fp16_opt, alt=int8_slow (alt_time ~= 2.3x)
kv_cache: hotset_miss 9% -> 44% around t=98s
latency_ms: p50=11 p95=94 p99=230
queue_wait_ms: avg=3.9 max=88
```

ken: Can you reproduce with a replay? which compat policy and routing header used?

maria: Repro steps: replay 45s steady mixed traffic: 65% short (<50 toks) + 35% long (350-500 toks). Route header: X-Variant-Mode: mixed. Compat policy: permissive with compat_window_ms=6 and token_budget_target=48.

sophia: Suspect batching slices split when fallback kicks in. Slices get drained mid-window, causing smaller final batches and forcing kernel conversion overhead. Two knobs: increase compat_window_ms or raise token_budget_target.

alex: Microbench confirms kernel switch cost fp16<->int8 includes reorder + dequant overhead; batches mixing quantizations see kernel latency x1.3-1.6.

sophia: Proposed canary config: 
```
queue_policy:
  compat_window_ms: 10
  token_budget_target: 72
  slice_grace_ms: 3
  prefer_compat_kernel_tags: true
```
This waits a bit longer and pushes for larger token packing.

maria: Ran a 15m canary with that config on pool gpu-a. Initial results: p99 down ~28% for traced workload, occupancy decreased from 7.1 -> 5.5 (throughput vs latency tradeoff). KV miss-rate dropped 46% -> 20%.

ken: Occupancy drop worries cost. Can we add kernel_tag metadata on variants so router can group by kernel compatibility and avoid mixing incompatible quantizations? e.g. kernel_tag: fp16 / int8.

alex: We have variant labels. Adding kernel_tag is straightforward. Router heuristic: prefer grouping by kernel_tag before broad compat relaxation. Risk: increased fragmentation => smaller batches unless token_budget offsets.

maria: Launched second canary combining kernel_tag grouping + token_budget_target=60 + compat_window_ms=8. 10m run: p95/p99 stable, occupancy ~6.1, cost +~2.8%.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed to pool gpu-a/canary-9 by @maria at 2026-03-16T10:21Z — monitoring -> #canaries

sam-sre: We'll watch adjacent pools for spillover. Also alerting thresholds adjusted for canary.

sophia: Next actions:
- maria: run 1h canary with traffic shadowing prod and upload full kernel traces + KV timelines
- alex: implement kernel_tag field and router pref heuristic behind flag
- ken: compute cost projection for token_budget change (48 -> 60) across pools and expected latency gains
- sam-sre: monitor pool spill and set temporary caps if needed

maria: Added trace ids batch-9123..9150. Full traces uploaded to gs://redwood-perf/canaries/2026-03-16/kerneltag-fallback. Ticket RWDT-5123 updated.

alex: Extra runtime optimization idea: reuse preallocated reorder buffers on kernel conversion to avoid alloc/GC stalls. I can prototype a lightweight buffer pool.

ken: Good. If 1h canary looks stable, we roll out config gated by 10% -> 50% traffic ramp and keep kernel_tag grouping behind the flag for quick rollback.

perf-bot: Next alert window scheduled post-canary; will post p95/p99 deltas and KV timeline overlays.

maria: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
